stories.title: Andrade's Entrance Companion Identified Following AEW Collision Appearance
stories.tldr: Independent wrestler Amaris Blair has been identified as one of the women who accompanied Andrade El Idolo to the ring during the September 5 episode of AEW Collision. Blair jokingly credited a great selfie for landing her the televised spot on national television. Meanwhile, Andrade successfully defended his National Championship against Gabe Kidd and addressed his upcoming AEW World Championship opportunity. El Idolo declared his intention to defend the national title every week while strategically waiting for the right moment to cash in his guaranteed world title shot.

stories.title: Tony Khan Spoke with Mike Tenay About AEW Appearance
stories.tldr: AEW President Tony Khan recently approached retired legendary wrestling commentator Mike Tenay about making an appearance on a potential AEW show in Mexico around mid-July, though a deal ultimately did not come together. Tenay, known famously as the voice of TNA for its first 12 years and for his extensive lucha libre expertise in WCW, has been retired since 2016. Despite his retirement, he continues to receive offers from major wrestling companies and recently turned down an opportunity to appear on the seventh season of Dark Side of the Ring.

stories.title: Deonna Purrazzo Expresses Interest in Match Against Britt Baker
stories.tldr: ROH Women’s Pure Champion Deonna Purrazzo has expressed strong interest in a match against Britt Baker following Baker's recent return to AEW at All In. Purrazzo revealed that Baker previously helped connect her with Tony Khan, leading to her own AEW debut in early 2024. Both competitors are currently active in their respective divisions, with Purrazzo recently defending her Pure Championship and Baker appearing on AEW programming.

stories.title: Tributes Pour In Following the Death of Former AEW Star Andy 'The Butcher' Williams
stories.tldr: Following his collapse during an independent wrestling event in Pennsylvania, former AEW star Andy "The Butcher" Williams has tragically passed away at the age of 48. Authorities and medical examiners confirmed his passing, prompting an overwhelming wave of grief and tributes from across the professional wrestling and heavy metal music communities. Friends and peers throughout the industry have since shared emotional memories celebrating his kindness, storytelling, and impact as both a trailblazing musician and a beloved locker room presence.

stories.title: RUSH Addresses AEW Absence and Upcoming Return
stories.tldr: AEW star Rush recently addressed his absence from television and missing the All In event while shutting down speculation of a move to AAA. In a recent livestream, Rush revealed that he expects to return to AEW programming within the next few weeks. He admitted to feeling disappointed about missing out on Wembley Stadium, but expressed deep gratitude to Tony Khan and stated he is using the time to train and stay ready.

stories.title: Celebrity Performances and Highlights from WWE Sunday Night's Main Event
stories.tldr: WWE Sunday Night's Main Event emanated from the State Farm Arena in Atlanta on September 6, 2026, featuring major celebrity performances, surprise returns, and dramatic in-ring action. The event kicked off with a live musical performance by Quavo and saw Lil Yachty successfully complete a five-minute challenge against Baron Corbin, paving the way for Trick Williams to capture the United States Championship. Meanwhile, the card was punctuated by high-profile matches, a production botch during a six-woman tag team match, and a mysterious phone call received by Paul Heyman following Bronson Reed's interference in the Oba Femi and Bron Breakker bout.

stories.title: Bronson Reed Returns and Ruins Bron Breakker vs. Oba Femi at SNME
stories.tldr: Bronson Reed made a surprise return at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event in Atlanta, interfering in the highly anticipated match between Bron Breakker and Oba Femi. Reed attacked Femi with a steel chair, causing a disqualification finish and halting a bout that was meant to determine the true future of the company. The interference marked the full reunion of the stable The Vision, with Reed, Breakker, Logan Paul, Austin Theory, and Maxxine Dupri standing tall after a brutal post-match beatdown featuring multiple Tsunamis and Spears. Reed had been sidelined for roughly six months following a distal bicep tear suffered in February.

stories.title: Trick Williams Wins WWE United States Title with Help from Lil Yachty at SNME
stories.tldr: Trick Williams recaptured the WWE United States Championship from Baron Corbin at Sunday Night's Main Event in Atlanta, Georgia. The title opportunity was earned after rapper Lil Yachty successfully survived a chaotic five-minute challenge against Corbin earlier in the broadcast. Despite severe outside interference, a brutal back-and-forth battle, and a strike with the championship belt, Williams ultimately countered the End of Days and hit the Trick Shot to secure his second reign with the title.

stories.title: Randy Orton Defeats Cody Rhodes at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event
stories.tldr: Randy Orton defeated Cody Rhodes in a chaotic and bloody headline match at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event after utilizing a low blow and a timely RKO. The intense rivalry, which reignited when Orton cost Rhodes the WWE Championship at SummerSlam, reached a boiling point in Atlanta with heavy involvement from Cody's family and multiple referee bumps. A pivotal moment occurred when Rhodes hesitated to deliver the Punt Kick after Orton begged for mercy, giving The Viper the opening he needed to steal the win. Fans are now heavily debating whether this dark display will lead to a massive heel turn for The American Nightmare.

stories.title: Lexis King and Former WWE NXT Talent Carolina Cruz Announce Engagement
stories.tldr: WWE NXT star Lexis King and former WWE talent Carolina Cruz have officially announced their engagement. King proposed to Cruz during a house party surrounded by friends, telling her that a wife was the only thing missing in his life before she happily accepted. The couple both previously spent time in WWE's developmental system after signing with the company in late 2023.

stories.title: Bret Hart Criticizes WWE Match Producers and Bruce Prichard
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Bret Hart recently criticized the current creative process in WWE during a podcast appearance, arguing that modern wrestlers lack the freedom he and his peers once enjoyed. Hart contrasted today's heavily produced environment with his own career, where he was largely trusted to construct iconic matches from start to finish. He blamed the product's perceived shortcomings on inexperienced individuals telling talent how to work. Furthermore, Hart specifically called out longtime WWE executive Bruce Prichard, stating bluntly that he does not know anything about wrestling.

stories.title: Tyler Breeze Reflects on WWE Main Roster Call-Up Concerns and Near Release
stories.tldr: Tyler Breeze recently revealed that he and Big Cass were originally scheduled to be fired during the filming of an ESPN E60 documentary in WWE developmental, but they managed to save their jobs by altering their career trajectories. Breeze also shared that he deeply dreaded his eventual main roster call-up because he was certain Vince McMahon would not understand or appreciate his gimmick. While he acknowledged the financial benefits of moving to Raw and SmackDown, Breeze preferred the passionate wrestling environment of NXT and felt his initial fears about the main roster were entirely validated.

stories.title: Zoey Stark Details Her Highest Payday from WWE Saudi Arabia Event
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Zoey Stark, now performing under the name Zoey Serrano, recently reflected on her 14-year professional wrestling career by sharing the stark contrasts in her earnings. While her early days on the independent circuit sometimes yielded no financial compensation beyond a handshake, her most lucrative payday came from competing in WWE. Specifically, Serrano revealed that her Fatal 4-Way match for the Women's World Championship at WWE Crown Jewel 2023 in Saudi Arabia netted her an insane amount of money that remains unmatched in her career.

stories.title: Undertaker and AJ Styles Working Backstage Roles for WWE NXT and AAA
stories.tldr: The Undertaker and AJ Styles recently took on significant backstage producer roles for major events across WWE NXT and AAA. During a busy weekend of wrestling, Undertaker helped put together a match at AAA Ola de Calor, while Styles was entrusted with the main event at NXT Heatwave. Additional backstage notes also revealed the complete list of producers and writers for recent television episodes of Raw and SmackDown.

stories.title: John Cena Explains Relationship with WWE Fans
stories.tldr: John Cena recently opened up about his complex history with the WWE fanbase during a recent media appearance. Despite enduring years of divisive mixed reactions and facing a notoriously critical audience, Cena expressed deep admiration for their unwavering attentiveness. He explained that performing for such a demanding crowd ultimately prepared him to transition into complex Hollywood acting roles that require intense character belief.

stories.title: Liv Morgan Sends Message Ahead of World Title Defense Against Stephanie Vaquer
stories.tldr: Liv Morgan delivered a confident promo during the Sunday Night Main Event Countdown show ahead of her Women's World Championship defense against Stephanie Vaquer on Monday Night Raw. Morgan mocked her challenger and declared that a victory would cement her legacy as the greatest champion of all time. The upcoming bout serves as a rematch of their WrestleMania 42 clash, where Morgan previously defeated Vaquer before an injury temporarily sidelined the challenger.

stories.title: Gene Snitsky Facial Hair Goes Viral
stories.tldr: Former WWE superstar Gene Snitsky is currently making waves on social media due to his impressively massive and unique new beard. The five-year wrestling veteran, who is famously remembered for his 2004 debut program with Kane and Lita, recently shared photos of his wild facial hair that have quickly spread across platforms like wildfire. Although it has been years since his full-time WWE run ending in late 2008, Snitsky recently made a one-off return appearance in 2023 and has also signed with Major League Wrestling.

stories.title: WWE Title Changes Teased for Upcoming Week
stories.tldr: WWE is heading into a massive week of action across Raw, SmackDown, NXT, and AAA featuring numerous high-profile championship matches. Several titles are predicted to change hands during major events in Mexico City and TripleMania. Meanwhile, outside interference and intense storyline rivalries are expected to protect several current champions from losing their gold. This upcoming stretch of television promises to significantly shake up the wrestling landscape.

stories.title: WWE Superstars Cast in Total Divas Reboot
stories.tldr: The hit reality series Total Divas could be successfully rebooted in 2026, offering a fresh behind the scenes look at the lives of modern WWE Superstars. This speculative casting list highlights five key acts, ranging from rising NXT talents like Tiffany Stratton and Izzi Dame to industry veteran Chelsea Green. The proposed revival would also bridge the gap between generations by incorporating original series trailblazers like The Bella Twins and Natalya.

stories.title: WWE Women's Royal Rumble 2027 Early Plans
stories.tldr: As WWE looks ahead to the Road to WrestleMania 43 and the 2027 Royal Rumble in Glendale, Arizona, the women's match remains wide open compared to the men's division. Three potential winners have emerged for the upcoming bout, including rising star Sol Ruca, who previously reached the final three in 2026. Other top contenders include former champions Bianca Belair and Naomi, both of whom are currently sidelined due to pregnancy but could make high-profile returns just in time for the Royal Rumble.

stories.title: WWE Tag Team Splitting Up Rumors
stories.tldr: Despite recent roster departures, WWE creative appears poised to break up several notable pairings across the men and women divisions. Damian Priest and R-Truth are heading toward a likely violent split following mounting tensions, while Tiffany Stratton is expected to seek payback against Chelsea Green after suffering injuries in her absence. Additionally, the brief alliance between Sami Zayn and Johnny Gargano is ending as Gargano trends back toward a solo babyface run.

stories.title: Early Betting Odds for WWE Money in the Bank 2026
stories.tldr: As WWE Money in the Bank 2026 approaches on October 10 from the Smoothie King Arena in New Orleans, attention turns to the women's division and several top stars who have never won the prestigious briefcase. The list of potential first-time winners includes decorated veterans like Charlotte Flair and Becky Lynch, rising talent Roxanne Perez, and former champion Rhea Ripley, who is currently recovering from knee surgery. Capturing the contract offers each of these competitors a unique pathway back into the championship picture or a fresh storyline catalyst.

stories.title: Trick Williams Recalls WWE NXT Segment with The Undertaker
stories.tldr: Trick Williams recently reflected on his memorable faceoff with WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker on NXT last year, which culminated in him taking a chokeslam in the center of the ring. Williams admitted that hearing The Undertaker's iconic gong drop made his heart sink, recalling how he was actually terrified of the legendary wrestler as a child playing video games. Despite the physical toll of the chokeslam, Williams remembers the encounter fondly and believes he earned The Undertaker's respect that night.

stories.title: Former WWE Stars Reportedly Looking to Re-Sign
stories.tldr: Despite having a packed roster across Raw, SmackDown, and NXT, WWE continues to look to its past by potentially bringing back several former talents like Eric Young, Killer Kross, Scarlett, and Enzo Amore. Eric Young has already made a cryptic cameo appearance training Lil Yachty after his TNA release, reportedly joining as a player/coach in NXT. Meanwhile, former stars like Killer Kross, Scarlett, and Enzo Amore are rumored as possible future returns following the recent comebacks of Baron Corbin and Big Cass.

stories.title: CM Punk Explains Working Recent WWE NXT Live Event
stories.tldr: Undisputed WWE Champion CM Punk recently surprised fans by appearing at an NXT live event in Petersburg, Virginia, teaming up with Myles Borne and Tavion Heights to defeat The Vanity Project. In a backstage vlog, Punk explained that his appearance was driven by a selfish desire to stay ready and get more reps in the ring, alongside a respect for giving back to the developmental brand. He praised the overall quality of the show, rated it exceptionally high, and confirmed his intention to return to NXT in the future. The event also featured a viral backstage confrontation between Punk and Grayson Waller, who jokingly told the champion he needed permission to wrestle on the brand.

stories.title: Ron Simmons Explains Origin of Catchphrase
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Ron Simmons recently discussed the organic origins of his famous catchphrase during a podcast appearance with his former APA partner JBL. Simmons explained that the single-word exclamation started as a spontaneous reaction to mistakes in the ring that fans in the front rows quickly picked up on. Creative eventually noticed the crowd interaction and booked him to use it on television during a segment involving Booker T and John Cena. The resulting massive crowd pop officially turned the simple utterance into an iconic Attitude Era staple.

stories.title: Push to Bring Back WWE Cruiserweight Classic
stories.tldr: TJ Perkins and fellow wrestler Lince Dorado recently rediscovered the original Cruiserweight Classic trophy while walking through a WWE storage warehouse. Inspired by the find and approaching the ten-year anniversary of the 2016 tournament, TJP revealed that he and multiple others have been actively pitching WWE on bringing the concept back. While WWE has not yet approved a revival, TJP hopes to see the tournament return, noting he would even be open to hosting rather than competing.

stories.title: Producers and Writers Listed for WWE Raw and SmackDown
stories.tldr: New backstage details reveal the producers and writers responsible for the matches and segments on recent episodes of WWE Raw and SmackDown. Veteran producers like Michael Hayes, Jamie Noble, Shane Helms, and Jason Jordan helped put together the August 31 episode of Raw. Meanwhile, the September 4 episode of SmackDown featured a main event between CM Punk and Johnny Gargano produced by Michael Hayes and Bobby Roode. The reports outline specific creative assignments for both shows, highlighting the teamwork behind major storylines and matches.

stories.title: Faction Inductees Teased for WWE Hall of Fame 2027
stories.tldr: As WWE continues to plan its future Hall of Fame classes ahead of schedule, speculation has begun regarding which legendary stables could be honored in 2027. Prominent factions like the Nation of Domination, The Wyatt Family, and Evolution have been highlighted as top contenders for induction. Each of these groups played a pivotal role in shaping different eras of professional wrestling and launching multiple legendary careers.

stories.title: Spike Dudley Recalls Iconic WWE Moment with The Undertaker
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Spike Dudley recently discussed an iconic moment from his career involving The Undertaker on Busted Open Radio. Dudley recalled pitching a dangerous chokeslam from inside the ring over the top rope to the outside floor, which The Undertaker initially flatly rejected out of concern for his safety. However, after Bubba Ray Dudley vouched for Spike's toughness, The Deadman agreed to give it a try. The resulting spot became one of the most memorable high-impact moments of Spike's career due to his diminutive size compared to the rest of the roster.

stories.title: WWE Superstars Rumored to Join Randy Orton Faction
stories.tldr: As Randy Orton prepares to face Cody Rhodes at Sunday Night’s Main Event in pursuit of his fifteenth world championship, speculation is rising that he may form a new heel faction. To bolster his chances, The Viper could recruit rising NXT and main roster talents to watch his back during his quest. Four specific wrestlers have emerged as the top candidates to potentially join this rumored stable.

stories.title: JBL Shares Thoughts on WWE Roster Cuts
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer John Bradshaw Layfield recently shared his perspective on WWE talent cuts, releases, and developmental salaries during an episode of Something to Wrestle. JBL defended the company's financial practices, noting that WWE takes significant risks and invests heavily in unproven talent through the NXT system. While acknowledging that modern developmental wages and old-school pay scales are like apples and oranges, he ultimately believes that current talent have it very good and that roster adjustments make business sense.

stories.title: Maven Clears Up Rumors Regarding Triple H
stories.tldr: Former WWE star Maven recently addressed rumors that he genuinely harbors ill will toward WWE Chief Content Officer Triple H due to his YouTube channel content. Appearing on the Rewind Recap Relive podcast, Maven explained that his online business actually thrives when the wrestling industry is booming and Triple H is succeeding. He admitted that while certain video thumbnails and topics might suggest personal beef to drive clicks, he is fully aware of the science behind content creation. Ultimately, Maven needs WWE and Hunter to operate at a high level because a healthy wrestling ecosystem directly benefits his channel's growth.

stories.title: Looking Back at Past Wrestling Rumors
stories.tldr: This weekly rumor review from early March 2026 examines how past reports played out regarding WrestleMania 42 plans and major roster moves. Key highlights include Danhausen’s surprise WWE debut at Elimination Chamber after his AEW contract expired, Seth Rollins getting cleared for a WrestleMania match against GUNTHER, and creative shifts involving Jade Cargill, Finn Balor, and Cody Rhodes. The report also touches on backstage news regarding Bronson Reed, AEW media rights stability, and impending roster departures.

stories.title: Chelsea Green Discusses Fan Perception Turning Point
stories.tldr: WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green credits the Netflix docuseries WWE Unreal as the turning point of her career, shifting fan perception from finding her annoying to deeply loving her. Behind-the-scenes footage and controversial remarks from Michael Hayes regarding her role in the company caused fans to rally behind her and force a natural babyface turn. Green now compares her organic rise to iconic movements like Daniel Bryan at WrestleMania 30 and KofiMania as she prepares for her first title defense against Nia Jax.

stories.title: Rumor Roundup and Faction Updates
stories.tldr: Royce Keys and OTM's new stable has officially been named 946 following a recent WWE trademark filing. Backstage reception to the group has been strongly positive, and they have already filmed new vignettes outside of Orlando to explain their alliance. Creative discussions are also underway regarding the possibility of adding a fourth member to the group in the future.

stories.title: Memphis Wrestling Legend 'Superstar' Bill Dundee Passes Away at 82
stories.tldr: Memphis wrestling legend Superstar Bill Dundee has passed away at the age of 82. His son, Jamie Dundee, confirmed that his father died at approximately 3:30 a.m. on Sunday, September 6, 2026. Dundee was celebrated for his storied career, particularly his legendary rivalry and tag team partnership with Jerry The King Lawler in the Memphis territory. Figures across the professional wrestling world, including WWE and numerous legends, shared heartfelt tributes honoring his immense legacy.

stories.title: Malakai Black Wins PROGRESS World Championship in Post-WWE Return
stories.tldr: Malakai Black captured the PROGRESS Men’s World Championship by defeating Cara Noir in the main event of PROGRESS The Odyssey Tour in Manchester, England. This victory marks Black's first championship since his WWE release in April and his first appearance for the promotion in roughly nine years, dating back to his time as Tommy End. The win brings an end to Cara Noir's 126-day title reign and establishes a major milestone for Black as he accelerates his prominent return to the independent wrestling scene.

stories.title: TNA's Santino Marella Wins Gold Medal at Jiu-Jitsu Con
stories.tldr: TNA Wrestling Director of Authority Santino Marella recently captured a gold medal at Jiu-Jitsu Con in Las Vegas. Representing Zenith BJJ, the former WWE star finished first in a field of five competitors in the Master 5 purple belt super heavyweight division. Marella took to social media after returning to Toronto to celebrate the victory while detailing the brutal physical toll the tournament took on his body. Despite dealing with injuries such as a misaligned jaw, a hurt back, and bleeding feet, he stated that winning gold made the painful experience entirely worthwhile.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff Discusses Wrestlers as 'Method Actors'
stories.tldr: Eric Bischoff recently discussed the concept of professional wrestlers acting as method actors by living their gimmicks twenty four seven. He highlighted legendary names like Hulk Hogan, Ric Flair, Stone Cold Steve Austin, and The Undertaker as prime examples of stars whose real personalities blurred with their television personas. Bischoff also pointed to modern stars like MJF and Roman Reigns, praising their absolute commitment and ability to generate authentic crowd reactions.

stories.title: Luther Stone Profiled as Supreme Wrestling Champion
stories.tldr: Luther Stone is making waves as the 22-year-old Supreme Heavyweight Champion, but his tough persona is deeply rooted in a real-life struggle for survival after being born prematurely following the loss of his twin. Drawing inspiration from childhood idol Nic Nemeth and relentless mentorship from veterans like Stephen Stone and Stephen Steel, he brings an unbreakable, aggressive spirit to the squared circle. As he continues to evolve his physical and mental preparation—while even learning the difficult art of being selfish—Stone views his championship not as his entire identity, but as proof of a lifetime overcoming the impossible.

stories.title: Tessa Blanchard Comments on Internet Wrestling Community
stories.tldr: Tessa Blanchard is continuing to make headlines as she navigates her latest career moves. In a recent interview, the outspoken wrestler opened up about the personal toll of public backlash. She specifically cited the internet wrestling community as one of the most difficult obstacles she has ever had to overcome.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite Rebel Heart special preview and card updates
stories.tldr: AEW is presenting the Rebel Heart special episode of Dynamite on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, from the Akins Ford Arena in Athens, Georgia, to honor Tanea Brooks, known as Rebel, following her terminal ALS diagnosis. The stacked card features Will Ospreay making his first match appearance as AEW World Champion in an eliminator match against David Finlay, alongside championship defenses and special segments. The night also marks Britt Baker's in-ring return in a six-woman tag team match and the revival of her talk show, The Waiting Room, alongside Steven Borden's in-ring debut.

stories.title: Mike Bailey discusses modern wrestling character work
stories.tldr: AEW wrestler Mike Bailey recently discussed the evolution of modern wrestling character work, arguing that the industry needs immersive personalities rather than traditional gimmicks restricted solely to weekly television. Bailey emphasized that modern wrestlers should embrace social media, transparency, and direct fan engagement to help the industry grow. He also explained that his active vlogging and Twitch streaming channels stem from a history of connecting with fans online, particularly during the pandemic and his five-year US travel ban.

stories.title: Alicia Atout celebrates first wedding anniversary with AEW's MJF
stories.tldr: AEW star MJF and broadcasting personality Alicia Atout are celebrating their first wedding anniversary after officially tying the knot on September 5, 2025. Their romance blossomed after years of trading insults in interviews and knowing each other since their early twenties, eventually leading to a relationship made official in late 2023. Despite early missed connections and an ignored first message, MJF persistence paid off when a double message finally secured their first date. Now, one year into marriage with guests like Taz and HOOK having attended their ceremony, the couple remains happily together as they reflect on their unique journey from friendly rivals to husband and wife.

stories.title: Emi Sakura set for upcoming MyAEW PPV card appearance
stories.tldr: AEW performer Emi Sakura is set to make her return to action after not wrestling in the company since September 2025. She will team with Killer Queens stablemate Suruga to face Anita Vaughan and Safire Reed at an upcoming Pro Wrestling EVE event. The show is titled Global Thunder Queens Attack and is scheduled for Friday, October 2nd. Fans can purchase the event as a one-off stream on the MyAEW platform or access it live through the EVE Champion Tier on YouTube.

stories.title: Rocky Romero details working as coordinator between AEW, NJPW, and CMLL
stories.tldr: Rocky Romero plays a crucial behind-the-scenes role as a coordinator managing the complex working relationships between AEW, New Japan Pro Wrestling, and CMLL. Appearing on What Happened When, Romero explained that balancing the full-time schedules of all three promotions is extremely demanding and requires constant communication. While much of the coordination happens online, he still travels frequently for AEW, CMLL, and New Japan events.

stories.title: Kris Statlander recalls starting AEW career during pandemic era
stories.tldr: Kris Statlander recently reflected on the unique challenges of starting her All Elite Wrestling career right as the COVID-19 pandemic began. Compounding the situation, she suffered a severe ACL tear in June 2020 that sidelined her for nine months and left her unable to walk at home. Despite these early hardships, she credited the supportive family environment within AEW for helping her recover and successfully return. Statlander ultimately overcame multiple knee injuries to capture both the TBS Championship and the AEW Women's World Championship.

stories.title: Will Ospreay opens up about dealing with body dysmorphia in NJPW
stories.tldr: AEW star Will Ospreay recently opened up about battling body dysmorphia during his early career in New Japan Pro Wrestling when he struggled with gym insecurities and harsh online criticism. After years of feeling too embarrassed to ask for help, he eventually discovered structured workout programs and hired a personal trainer to understand nutrition and weight training. This pivotal change allowed him to transform his physique in a healthy way and build lasting confidence. Today, he stands as one of the top athletes in professional wrestling and a major champion in All Elite Wrestling.

stories.title: Tag Team Chicago Street Fight match set for AEW All Out 2026
stories.tldr: The AEW All Out 2026 lineup is growing with the addition of a violent women's tag team championship rematch. Women's Tag Team Champions The Brawling Birds will defend their titles against Divine Dominion in a Chicago Street Fight. Additionally, Will Ospreay will put the AEW World Championship on the line against Jon Moxley at the September 26 event.

stories.title: New Level (Kofi Kingston & Austin Creed) discuss AEW transition and name origin
stories.tldr: Following their surprise AEW debut and World Trios Championship win, Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed have shed light on their rapid signing timeline and the inspiration behind their new name, New Level. The duo officially put pen to paper on August 29 after meeting with Tony Khan the week prior. Creed has since celebrated a whirlwind week that featured their first Dynamite title defense and his 40th birthday.

stories.title: Motor City Machine Guns pick up first victory since signing with AEW
stories.tldr: The Motor City Machine Guns have secured their first victory as officially signed AEW talent. Alex Shelley and Chris Sabin defeated The Swirl on Collision. The duo is now firmly positioned in the championship picture following their recent arrival.

stories.title: Trent Beretta revives old Kofi Kingston post following Kingston's AEW arrival
stories.tldr: While Kofi Kingston settles into his new home in AEW, he is already facing some renewed attention from a locker room colleague with a long memory. Trent Beretta recently resurfaced a brutal social media post from 2013 where he insulted Kingston following his own past WWE departure. Beretta shared the old message alongside a sarcastic corporate tagline, leaving fans wondering if a real grudge has been reignited.

stories.title: Debate over Mercedes Moné's standing in American women's wrestling history
stories.tldr: The debate over Mercedes Mone's historical standing has intensified as Dave Meltzer declared her the best overall in-ring worker among American women in history. Meltzer also placed her alongside Becky Lynch as the leading active candidates for the Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame. However, historical voting trends show that active wrestlers still face a steep climb to reach the required sixty percent threshold for induction.

stories.title: Andrade discusses future AEW World Title shot following Collision
stories.tldr: Following his Casino Gauntlet victory at All In, Andrade El Idolo has officially secured a guaranteed AEW World Championship match whenever he chooses to use it. During the September 5 episode of Collision, after successfully defending the National Championship against Gabe Kidd, Andrade revealed he is holding onto the contract for now. Instead of immediately challenging Will Ospreay, the National Champion plans to bide his time and cash in when the timing is right.

stories.title: Speculation on former WWE stars joining United Empire in AEW
stories.tldr: Following Will Ospreay's announcement of a new AEW iteration of the United Empire, speculation has grown regarding which free agents and recently departed talent might join the group. Potential recruits include former WWE stars Ilja Dragunov, Aleister Black, Sheamus, and Tonga Loa, all of whom recently parted ways with their previous promotion. Integrating these veterans could provide Ospreay's faction with immediate star power and NJPW authenticity as it launches on AEW television.

stories.title: Will Ospreay reflects on journey to becoming a pro wrestler
stories.tldr: Will Ospreay recently shared the unexpected influences that shaped his path to becoming a professional wrestler. From watching television with his father to learning timing at his mother's drama academy, his early days laid a unique foundation. He also studied high flying maneuvers on a trampoline before eventually finding his footing at the London School of Lucha Libre.

stories.title: Maya World credits Athena for preparing her for AEW breakout
stories.tldr: Maya World recently credited her trainer and former rival Athena with preparing her for her breakout run in All Elite Wrestling. In a recent interview, World highlighted how Athena not only trained her at the DFW All-Pro Wrestling Academy but also instilled the crucial mindset of staying constantly prepared for big opportunities. World's remarks come as she recovers from losing the TBS Championship to Persephone at All In following interference from Britt Baker.

stories.title: AJ Lee addresses future in pro wrestling following WWE WrestleMania 42
stories.tldr: Following her loss of the Women’s Intercontinental Championship to Becky Lynch at WrestleMania 42, AJ Lee addressed her professional wrestling future and clarified that her recent return is not a definitive farewell. In subsequent interviews, she admitted that the run reminded her of her in-ring capabilities and left her open to future appearances. However, any potential return will depend heavily on whether a fresh, story-driven opportunity presents itself that genuinely excites her. In the meantime, she plans to focus on her writing while staying physically prepared for whatever comes next.

stories.title: Labor Day analysis on WWE wrestler pay and unionization
stories.tldr: This editorial argues that WWE wrestlers are severely underpaid and exploited by the TKO corporate hierarchy while executives rake in tens of millions of dollars. Despite generating record revenues, wrestlers are facing steep pay cuts that have already driven acts like the New Day to request their releases. The piece asserts that the roster holds all the real power and should consider unionizing and staging a walkout to leverage their value against corporate greed. Fans would likely support such a movement given widespread anger over TKO's pricing and streaming practices.

stories.title: Trish Stratus recalls WWE rebuilding women's division after Chyna's departure
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Trish Stratus recently discussed the challenging period the women's division faced following Chyna's departure in 2001. With Chyna leaving as the champion, the division essentially had to be rebuilt from scratch around emerging talents like Stratus and Lita. Stratus recalled how key additions like Jazz and Molly Holly helped revitalize the locker room, culminating in a historic six-pack challenge at Survivor Series where she won her first Women's Championship.

stories.title: John Cena reflects on Netflix's WWE Unreal series
stories.tldr: John Cena recently admitted that he and many other WWE performers were initially apprehensive about pulling back the curtain for the Netflix docuseries WWE Unreal. However, the show's undeniable success across multiple seasons forced Cena to realize that the wrestling business has changed and that he needed to adapt alongside it. The project ultimately provided Cena with a valuable platform to share his personal perspective on controversial moments from his retirement tour, including his heel turn and matches with Brock Lesnar. Now, Cena is grateful for the opportunity to explain his creative convictions and even hopes to expand on the storytelling of his final run in the future.

stories.title: WWE planning to add female stars to current factions
stories.tldr: WWE is reportedly planning to integrate more female stars into its existing male-dominated factions to increase mixed-gender group dynamics on television. Current stables like The Vision, Birthright, 946, and Los Perros Del Mal are highlighted as prime candidates for these additions. Speculated roster moves and new signees include Jordynne Grace, Marie Malenko, Jaida Parker, and Xena joining various stables.

stories.title: Search continues for WWE's next Rey Mysterio
stories.tldr: WWE continues its long-standing search for the next Rey Mysterio as the legendary luchador approaches four decades in the business and remains active on television. While many masked signings have failed to capture his unique magic, several current roster members and recent acquisitions are positioned as potential successors. Contenders range from established stars like Dragon Lee, Penta, and Rey Fenix to internal legacy figures like Dominik Mysterio and various masked international talents.

stories.title: WWE Men's Royal Rumble 2027 early winner plans
stories.tldr: With WWE setting the 2027 Royal Rumble in Glendale, Arizona, early speculation has begun regarding potential winners for the marquee match. Dominant powerhouse Oba Femi emerges as the clear frontrunner following a stellar run that includes winning the King of the Ring tournament. Meanwhile, veteran fan favorites Sami Zayn and LA Knight round out the top early contenders with compelling storylines leading toward WrestleMania 43.

stories.title: WWE star Angelo Dawkins welcomes new baby girl
stories.tldr: WWE star Angelo Dawkins and his partner Grace Russo have welcomed their third child, a baby girl, making them a family of five. The couple shared the happy news on Instagram with photos from the hospital following her arrival on September 5, 2026. This comes several months after they initially announced the pregnancy in March, joking that they were about to be officially outnumbered by their growing household.

stories.title: WWE Hall of Famer character gets live-action movie teaser
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Robert Remus, known as Sgt. Slaughter, has announced that a live-action movie based on his iconic military persona is currently in development. Titled Slaughter: The Origin Story, the project will feature a younger version of the character and is set in 1983, following a drill instructor facing a hostage crisis on Diablo Island. Remus is serving as executive producer and has already released an early teaser scene for his wrestling and G.I. Joe fanbase. While cast details and a release date have not yet been announced, the film marks a new chapter for a character with deep historical ties to both professional wrestling and the G.I. Joe franchise.

stories.title: JBL and Ron Simmons recall hitting Shane McMahon in WWE
stories.tldr: During a recent interview, APA members JBL and Ron Simmons recalled a terrifying moment when they legitimately thought they were fired from WWE. JBL delivered an exceptionally brutal Clothesline From Hell to Shane McMahon after McMahon specifically asked to be hit as hard as possible. Simmons immediately told JBL to start packing his bags because he was certain the heavy blow would cost them their jobs. Fortunately, McMahon was thrilled with the segment and unharmed, validating the veterans' commitment to realism in the ring.

stories.title: WWE return plans for Drew McIntyre
stories.tldr: Drew McIntyre has been absent from WWE television since his Street Fight against Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 while spending the summer filming international projects. Following his return to the United States, speculation has grown regarding how the Scottish Psychopath will be reintroduced to programming. Analysts have mapped out six potential return scenarios, ranging from targeting Cody Rhodes and The Bloodline to Hollywood-inspired character shifts and interfering with CM Punk.

stories.title: Jacy Jayne reflects on NXT lessons following main roster call-up
stories.tldr: WWE main roster star Jacy Jayne recently reflected on her extensive developmental run in NXT during an appearance on Notsam Wrestling, crediting her time in the brand for her current success, including her Women's United States Championship victory in August. Jayne acknowledged that she was not actually ready for a call-up years ago and thanked Shawn Michaels for keeping her in NXT to hone her craft. She explained how making mistakes and dealing with hostile crowds in NXT ultimately prepared her to lead Fatal Influence and handle high-pressure situations on the main roster.

stories.title: Kevin Nash recalls overcoming tough injury during 2000s WWE run
stories.tldr: Wrestling legend Kevin Nash recently reflected on his grueling 2000s WWE run during his Kliq This podcast, focusing on a severe quad tear he suffered at age 42. He shared details about being confined to a wheelchair for over 40 days and how compensating for the injury ultimately caused severe shoulder problems due to his 340-pound frame. Nash also noted that seeing his longtime friend Triple H go through the exact same injury a year prior provided a helpful roadmap for his own recovery, though he humorously regretted not being a more attentive friend at the time.

stories.title: Eric Bischoff believes Undertaker's WrestleMania streak should have stayed intact
stories.tldr: Former wrestling executive Eric Bischoff recently stated on his podcast that The Undertaker should have retired with his iconic WrestleMania undefeated streak intact rather than having Brock Lesnar break it at WrestleMania 30. Bischoff argued that breaking the streak provided no necessary career boost for Lesnar, who was already immensely popular, and missed a rare chance to cement Undertaker as the immortal Babe Ruth of professional wrestling. Dismissing the traditional wrestling custom of putting over younger talent as outdated country boy bullshit, Bischoff believes keeping the streak alive would have created a truly unique legacy.

stories.title: Sol Ruca reflects on adjustment to WWE main roster
stories.tldr: Following her call-up to the WWE main roster in April and her subsequent run with the Women's Intercontinental Championship, Sol Ruca has opened up about the challenges of transitioning from NXT. She highlights that adjusting to a brand new crowd every week on the road is vastly different from performing in front of a familiar audience. Despite the learning curve and mixed crowd reactions, she is embracing the global scale of her new platform while continuing to work her way back to the championship picture.

stories.title: Bully Ray criticizes WWE main roster tag division and suggests mixed tag titles
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray recently expressed heavy criticism of the promotion's current main roster tag team division, arguing that the championships frequently lack meaningful storylines and feel secondary. Despite a recent influx of new pairings and reported plans for a division refresh, Ray remains skeptical that traditional tag team wrestling will improve anytime soon. Instead, he proposed the creation of a permanent mixed tag team division featuring male and female pairings, which he believes would inject fresh excitement and storytelling potential into the company.

stories.title: John Cena names his top five favorite WWE t-shirt designs
stories.tldr: During a recent Q&A at Fan Expo Canada, wrestling legend John Cena revealed his top five favorite t-shirt designs from his extensive WWE career. Ranging from his colorful character eras to his recent retirement tour, Cena highlighted shirts featuring a Super Mario parody, a G.I. Joe design, and his meaningful charitable initiatives. He also pointed out hidden messages in his farewell merchandise as a favorite detail.

stories.title: Kevin Nash explains why he only cared about his first World Title win
stories.tldr: WWE Hall of Famer Kevin Nash recently revealed on his podcast that he had no desire to win other world titles like the NWA or TNA championships during his career. Nash explained that his primary goal upon entering the business was simply to win the WWE Championship to secure a good position in the industry. Although he went on to win the WCW World Heavyweight Championship five times, he admitted he barely remembers those subsequent victories compared to his historic 1994 win as Diesel.

stories.title: Chad Gable credits amateur wrestling background for powering through Shorty G gimmick
stories.tldr: WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable recently discussed how his background in amateur wrestling helped him endure and succeed despite being given unfavorable creative directions, such as the unpopular Shorty G gimmick. Gable explained that the resilience and work ethic required to reach the Olympics and win national championships taught him to push through difficult professional phases even when he disagreed with them. While acknowledging that pro wrestling differs from amateur wrestling because hard work alone does not guarantee success and some decisions are out of his control, he maintains a patient and dedicated mindset. By treating the pro wrestling journey as a long-term process, he was able to stay focused, accept the challenges, and ultimately reach a much better position in his career.

stories.title: Preview, odds, and ticket updates for WWE Sunday Night's Main Event 2026
stories.tldr: Betting odds, ticket sales figures, and creative speculation have surfaced ahead of the upcoming event in Atlanta. Randy Orton, Oba Femi, Lil Yachty, and the trio of Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, and Tatum Paxley lead the latest betting lines. Meanwhile, ticket distributions have reached 10,237 as anticipation grows for potential surprise returns and shocking alliances.

stories.title: Reactions and backstage shock surrounding NXT releases including Wendy Choo and Adriana Rizzo
stories.tldr: Following WWE's recent developmental roster cuts, backstage reactions have surfaced highlighting widespread surprise over Wendy Choo's departure. Released talents including Adriana Rizzo have issued emotional statements addressing their exits after battling significant injuries during their tenure. Additional names involved in the mass release have also been fully confirmed by backstage reports.

stories.title: Johnny Gargano makes WWE SmackDown return and issues statement after loss to CM Punk
stories.tldr: Following his return and loss to CM Punk on SmackDown, Johnny Gargano released an emotional social media statement reflecting on the milestone. He admitted he is still a work in progress after months of self-doubt and promised this is only the beginning of a new chapter. Analysts and fans are already looking ahead to his next steps, which could include a partnership or feud with Sami Zayn, a pursuit of the United States Championship, or a run at Money in the Bank.

stories.title: Kelani Jordan sets record and discusses NXT Women's Championship and wedding
stories.tldr: Following a period of creative uncertainty, newly crowned NXT Women's Champion Kelani Jordan revealed that her title win over Kendal Grey set a record for the longest non-stipulation women's singles match. Celebrating her flawless track record of winning every championship on her first try, she has adopted the new nickname One Shot Lani. Additionally, Jordan discussed her upcoming wedding to Carmelo Hayes, confirming that while no wrestling antics or broken tables are planned, her championship belt will receive its own reserved front-row seat.

stories.title: John Cena proposes 36-date docuseries on his WWE farewell tour
stories.tldr: Building on his recent reflections about his 2025 farewell tour, John Cena is hoping to develop an extensive 36-date docuseries. Inspired by his experience filming the Netflix series WWE Unreal, Cena envisions a project where he walks fans through every stop of his final run. He hopes to provide his personal perspective on heavily debated choices like his final match finish and his squash by Brock Lesnar.

stories.title: Netflix edits Paige and Nikki Bella backstage segment from WWE SmackDown
stories.tldr: Netflix has edited the controversial backstage segment between Paige and Nikki Bella by removing a suggestive John Cena reference from its platform. While the USA Network broadcast aired the line unedited, the streaming version cut away to a crowd shot. This marks the latest in a growing trend of platform-specific censorship for WWE programming on the streaming service.

stories.title: Becky Lynch selects three matches that best represent her WWE career
stories.tldr: Continuing her recent podcast reflections, Becky Lynch has revealed the three matches that she believes best define her storied WWE career. She selected her WrestleMania 38 bout against Bianca Belair, her 2019 Hell in a Cell match against Sasha Banks, and a recent mixed tag match alongside her husband Seth Rollins. Outside of her podcast appearances, Lynch also remains heavily involved in the current Raw women championship picture alongside Stephanie Vaquer.

stories.title: Mickie James recalls scrapped WWE debut as CM Punk's manager
stories.tldr: Before her famous run involving Trish Stratus, Mickie James nearly made her WWE television debut under a completely different gimmick and era. She recently revealed that creative plans once positioned her to debut on Sunday Night Heat as CM Punk's manager named Vicky Adams. Although that plan and several others were ultimately scrapped, James eventually debuted in late 2005 to launch her historic main roster career.

stories.title: John Cena discusses Cody Rhodes passing the torch at SummerSlam
stories.tldr: John Cena is expanding on his final WWE chapter by addressing his dynamic and eventual torch-passing moment with Cody Rhodes. Cena admitted that Rhodes ultimately surpassed him, tracing Cody's journey from leaving the company to returning as a global star. He also drew parallels between their on-screen rivalry and a new Clash of Clans promotional campaign where Rhodes leads a hunt for Cena's base.

stories.title: Mickie James recalls bringing TNA Knockouts Championship to 2022 WWE Royal Rumble
stories.tldr: Mickie James nearly turned down her 2022 WWE Royal Rumble appearance due to anger over her previous release, but ultimately agreed on the condition that she could represent TNA. In a new interview, she revealed that she also had to fight to use her Hardcore Country persona and fend off a last-minute attempt by WWE to ban the TNA championship. James ultimately entered the match at number 22 and was eliminated by Lita.

stories.title: WWE plans for new member in '946' faction with Royce Keys and OTM
stories.tldr: Royce Keys recently formed the 946 stable on Raw alongside OTM members Bronco Nima and Lucien Price, quickly establishing dominance by attacking top roster stars. New updates reveal that Keys handpicked the duo and will serve as the sole leader of the faction. While the group currently stands at three members, creative plans leave the door open for the stable to expand in the future.

stories.title: Mickie James reveals almost quitting wrestling before major WWE storyline
stories.tldr: Beyond her recent Royal Rumble hesitations, Mickie James nearly walked away from the business much earlier during her developmental days in OVW. Frustrated by seeing friends fired and non-wrestlers prioritized over traditional talent, she contemplated quitting before taking acting classes and trying to adapt. After interventions from Tommy Dreamer and her mother, she stayed and brainstormed the iconic superfan character that launched her main roster career.

stories.title: Alexa Bliss discusses how working with Bray Wyatt shifted her perspective
stories.tldr: Alexa Bliss recently expanded on how her partnership with the late Bray Wyatt revolutionized her approach to character development in WWE. She explained that Wyatt taught her to build an entire universe and backstory for her persona rather than just focusing on standard promos. Bliss also shared how she continues to honor his memory on-screen, most recently paying tribute to him with a special gear choice at WrestleMania 42.

stories.title: Royce Keys issues warning following Bloodline attack on WWE TV
stories.tldr: Following a series of brutal assaults on The Bloodline and other WWE stars by the newly formed stable 946, leader Royce Keys has broken his silence. Keys and his allies released an Instagram vignette warning that nobody is safe from their wrath. The group officially confirmed their moniker 946 and stressed that their violent campaign is driven by loyalty rather than family ties.

stories.title: Grayson Waller discusses main roster perception vs. NXT success
stories.tldr: Following his NXT Championship victory at Heatwave, Grayson Waller opened up about feeling creatively stifled during his time on the main roster. He revealed that management only viewed him as a silly talk show host rather than letting him showcase his true abilities on the microphone. Waller confessed to severe nervousness during his return promo after going two years without a live TV microphone, but ultimately rediscovered his confidence. The newly crowned champion even boldly claimed to be a better talker than top main roster stars like Roman Reigns and CM Punk.

stories.title: Andy 'The Butcher' Williams collapses during independent wrestling event
stories.tldr: Andy Williams, known as The Butcher from his time in AEW and on the independent scene, suffered a medical emergency and collapsed at the end of his match during an Enjoy Wrestling event in Millvale, Pennsylvania. On-site medical staff and paramedics administered CPR and used a defibrillator before rushing him to the hospital, leading the promotion to cancel the remainder of the show. While unverified rumors regarding his condition circulated online, Enjoy Wrestling directly disputed false claims and stated they were at the hospital awaiting official updates.

stories.title: Pro wrestling legend Jerry Oates passes away at 81
stories.tldr: Professional wrestling veteran and territorial standout Jerry Oates has passed away at the age of 81. The Cauliflower Alley Club announced the sad news on Saturday morning, sharing a heartfelt statement provided by the Oates family. During a distinguished career spanning from 1970 to 2010, Oates captured multiple championships and found great success in tag team action alongside legends like Ronnie Garvin and Jesse Ventura. Beyond the ring, he was a dedicated gym owner, event promoter, and law enforcement officer who left a lasting, positive impact on his community.

stories.title: Bollywood Boyz report no recent offers from WWE or AEW
stories.tldr: Former WWE stars The Bollywood Boyz recently revealed that they have received zero offers from major promotions like WWE or AEW over the last few years. Operating primarily on the independent circuit since their 2021 departure from WWE as The Singh Brothers, the duo remains confident in their abilities and value. They also expressed gratitude for past opportunities to work AEW and Ring of Honor tapings while maintaining that they can fit into any tag team division today.

stories.title: Top pro wrestling matches in history for September 5
stories.tldr: September 5 has played host to numerous classic professional wrestling matches throughout history, spanning promotions like AEW, AJPW, Dragongate, and more. According to Cagematch ratings and Wrestling Observer Newsletter star ratings, the top-ranked match on this date is the legendary steel cage tag team title bout between The Young Bucks and Lucha Brothers from AEW All Out 2021. Dave Meltzer awarded that incredible encounter 5.75 stars, praising its relentless action, innovative spots, and dramatic near-falls.

stories.title: WCW Fall Brawl '91 retrospectives and classic match reviews
stories.tldr: A retro look back at a September 1991 World Championship Wrestling television special highlights a bout widely considered one of the worst matches in the promotion history. Van Hammer faced Terrence Taylor in a 67 second disaster featuring a egregiously botched finishing move. Prominent industry journalist Dave Meltzer famously rated the encounter negative two stars, declaring that it perfectly encapsulated everything wrong with professional wrestling. Fans today can still track down and watch this infamous piece of wrestling history through official archival video platforms.

stories.title: Pro wrestling title changes on September 5 in history
stories.tldr: September 5 is historically a slower day for professional wrestling title changes, with around 186 notable changes recorded on this date. Despite the slower pace, several significant championships have changed hands over the decades across major promotions. Notable historical winners include legendary tag teams and singles competitors in organizations like WCW, AJPW, WWE, and NJPW.

stories.title: Awesome Kong explains how she started her professional wrestling career
stories.tldr: Former professional wrestling star Awesome Kong recently reflected on her nearly two-decade career spanning TNA, AEW, and WWE. She shared how watching matches with foster children and observing Trish Stratus inspired her to enter the business despite facing early rejection. Motivated by critics who doubted her, Kong bet on herself, traveled to Japan, and built a storied legacy in the industry.

stories.title: AAA Triplemania 34 match announcements and show updates
stories.tldr: Following earlier card announcements, AAA has added more high-profile bouts to the upcoming Triplemania 34 two-night event. The War Raiders have issued an open challenge for their AAA World Tag Team Titles, and La Parka will defend the AAA Latin American Championship in a triple threat match against Laredo Kid and Mr. Iguana on Night One in Las Vegas. Additional matches and stipulations continue to flesh out the cards for both the Las Vegas and Mexico City shows.

stories.title: Matt Hardy addresses TNA locker room after Lockdown main event time cut
stories.tldr: Following the Lockdown pay-per-view, Matt Hardy held a meeting with the TNA locker room at subsequent TV tapings to address how earlier matches running long forced their main event cage match to have its time cut. Hardy used the podcast to emphasize the importance of roster professionalism, urging wrestlers to shave time from their own matches to protect the main event. Additionally, Hardy noted that Jeff Hardy missed those same television tapings due to ongoing travel issues entering Canada, which required TNA to temporarily write him off television using an injury angle.

stories.title: Praise for Mercedes Mone as one of the all-time best American women's wrestlers
stories.tldr: Following her AEW Women’s World Championship victory over Willow Nightingale at All In and a subsequent five-star match rating from Dave Meltzer, Mercedes Mone has sparked Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame discussions. Meltzer highlighted her historic resume, including holding titles across major global promotions and competing in legendary venues like the Tokyo Dome. Although no American woman has ever been voted into the Hall of Fame, Meltzer praised Mone as likely the best overall worker in the history of American women's wrestling. He also noted that Becky Lynch deserves consideration for briefly being the biggest star in the entire industry.

stories.title: AEW granted legal extension in ongoing dispute with Ryan Nemeth
stories.tldr: AEW has been granted a legal extension until December 2, 2026, to serve former wrestler Ryan Nemeth with papers after accusing him of evading the legal process. The ongoing legal dispute began when Nemeth filed a 2025 lawsuit against AEW, Tony Khan, and CM Punk regarding alleged threats and contract issues, prompting AEW to push for private arbitration in Florida. A judge also warned Nemeth that he could face financial penalties and attorney fees if he refuses to sign the requested service waiver without good cause.

stories.title: AEW Dynamite viewership numbers for September 2, 2026
stories.tldr: AEW Dynamite experienced a slight viewership increase on September 2, 2026, pulling in 796,000 viewers on TBS with a 0.21 rating in the key P18-49 demographic compared to the previous week. This performance also marked a massive year-over-year improvement of nearly 69 percent in total viewership and over 90 percent in the demo compared to early September 2025. These linear television metrics highlight continued growth as the promotion builds toward its next major live event.

stories.title: Justin Roberts pokes fun at his AEW All In ring announcing mistake
stories.tldr: Longtime AEW ring announcer Justin Roberts playfully addressed a mistake he made during the Casino Gauntlet match at AEW All In: London at Wembley Stadium. He accidentally introduced Komander as Mistico before quickly correcting himself right after Komander executed a trademark rope-running springboard dive. Amusingly, Mistico actually was the very next entrant in the match, making the timing of the slip-up quite funny. Roberts later took to social media to poke fun at the incident by sharing a photo standing alongside both luchadors with clear labels.

stories.title: Reason behind changing AEW Redemption main event from Omega vs MJF
stories.tldr: The original main event for AEW Redemption 2026 was supposed to feature Kenny Omega challenging MJF for the AEW World Championship. However, creative plans shifted because MJF needed time to heal from a hyperextended knee injury ahead of All In. Additionally, management wanted to put the belt on Omega early to market his massive title match against Will Ospreay at Wembley Stadium, which immediately boosted ticket sales. Ultimately, Ospreay defeated Omega at the event in front of a reported turnstile count of 41,102 fans to capture the championship.

stories.title: Google and YouTube search trends for AEW All In vs NXT Heatwave vs AAA
stories.tldr: A recent analysis of Google and YouTube search trends compared fan interest for AEW All In, NXT Heatwave, and AAA Ola de Calor, all of which took place on Sunday, August 30. The data revealed that AEW All In generated the highest search interest in the United States, outperforming both NXT and AAA across the weekend and into the following week. However, when WWE was included as a baseline comparison, WWE maintained its overall market dominance on both platforms, particularly with strong engagement for Monday Night Raw.

stories.title: AEW All In 2026 PPV buy estimates and critical reception
stories.tldr: Early estimates indicate that All In 2026 could break AEW's all-time pay-per-view buy record with projections ranging between 210,000 and 230,000 buys. Both domestic and international orders surged significantly over the company's 2026 averages, fueling what is now AEW's most successful six-month stretch in history. Wrestling legend Jim Ross also praised the event as the finest broadcast the promotion has ever produced, while the roster immediately turns its focus toward the upcoming All Out pay-per-view.

stories.title: Tay Melo refutes retirement rumors amid unclear AEW status
stories.tldr: Tay Melo has directly refuted recent speculation that she has quietly retired from professional wrestling. Fans initially suspected she hung up her boots after she removed the word wrestler from her Instagram bio. Melo quickly shut down those rumors on social media by stating she is not done in the ring yet, even as her official AEW release status remains unclear following her request to step away earlier this summer.

stories.title: Debate over Kenny Omega vs Will Ospreay match ratings and Ric Flair's comments
stories.tldr: The debate comparing Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay to Ric Flair and Ricky Steamboat has expanded as Jim Ross criticized Flair's defensive remarks as unnecessary. Flair quickly fired back at Ross, maintaining his right to defend his legacy against comparisons. Meanwhile, analysts continue to dissect the fundamental differences between modern and territory-era wrestling, citing major shifts in crowd psychology and wrestler scheduling.

stories.title: AEW's Andrade El Idolo exchanges social media posts with WWE's Carmelo Hayes
stories.tldr: Following his recent controversial comments regarding WWE favoring Samoan talent, AEW star Andrade El Idolo has continued to stir the pot on social media. His remarks prompted a sharp retort from The Usos regarding drawing power in the company. Now, Andrade has publicly questioned the whereabouts of former rival Carmelo Hayes due to the WWE star's recent lack of television time.

stories.title: Rush shuts down AAA return rumors, reaffirms commitment to AEW
stories.tldr: AEW star Rush recently addressed missing the All In 2026 event at Wembley Stadium while remaining absent from television since July. Amid fan speculation regarding his future, a suggestion was made for him to join the WWE-owned AAA promotion. Rush swiftly shut down the idea, making it clear that his loyalty and focus remain entirely with AEW.

stories.title: AEW Championship contenders set following post-All In Dynamite
stories.tldr: Following All In, the post-pay-per-view episode of AEW Dynamite established several major championship feuds and challengers moving forward. Newly crowned World Champion Will Ospreay immediately found himself targeted by Jon Moxley, Ricochet, Gabe Kidd, and MJF. Meanwhile, other divisions took shape with a major TLC tag team match announced, alongside returns and confrontations across the men and women divisions.

stories.title: New Level reportedly sign long-term deals with AEW following Dynamite debut
stories.tldr: Following their recent AEW debut as New Level, Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed have quickly established themselves as part of the World Trios Champions. According to reports, the duo has likely signed long-term deals with the company rather than waiting for a potential WWE return. Tony Khan also revealed that contract talks only began after their non-compete clauses expired, noting he had previously strengthened the divisions without anticipating their availability.

stories.title: Preview and breakdown of tag team matches for AEW All Out
stories.tldr: Adam Copeland and Christian Cage will defend their AEW World Tag Team Championships against FTR and the Young Bucks at All Out in a chaotic Tables and Ladders and Chairs match. Rather than quickly passing the belts around in a hot potato fashion, historical booking patterns suggest the champions will retain their titles to anchor the division. This sets up a dominant, long-term reign featuring fresh matchups against newly arrived tag teams like the Motor City Machine Guns and the New Level heading toward the winter.

stories.title: AEW star questions current booking of former WWE rival
stories.tldr: AEW National Champion Andrade has publicly questioned the current WWE booking of his former rival Carmelo Hayes. Taking to social media, Andrade asked his former opponent where he is due to Hayes missing recent television time. Hayes has not appeared on SmackDown since losing a United States Championship match to Baron Corbin, causing his main roster momentum to stall.

stories.title: Wrestling Weekly discussion on AEW All In fallout and Roman Reigns
stories.tldr: Les Thatcher and Vic Sosa discussed AEW's rapid turnaround from All In to All Out on their latest podcast. The hosts also shifted focus to WWE to examine Bayley's potential return. Additionally, they analyzed Roman Reigns upcoming challenger in Mexico City and recent developments within The Bloodline.

stories.title: Dave Meltzer awards Kenny Omega vs Will Ospreay 6.5 stars at AEW All In
stories.tldr: Dave Meltzer has officially awarded Will Ospreay and Kenny Omega's AEW All In World Championship match a staggering 6.5 stars. Meltzer praised the bout as the second-best match he has ever watched and called it the best complete match presentation in wrestling history. This rating adds another critical milestone to their storied rivalry following recent discussions by wrestling legends regarding their classic encounters.

stories.title: Jeff Jarrett Says This AEW Babyface Has A 'Unique' Charisma
stories.tldr: Wrestling veteran Jeff Jarrett recently praised AEW star Willow Nightingale on his podcast for possessing a rare and genuine connection with the audience. Jarrett highlighted that fans do not just enjoy watching Nightingale perform, but actively yearn for her to succeed in the ring. He defined this quality as the true essence of a classic babyface performer. This discussion adds to the ongoing industry praise surrounding Nightingale's enduring popularity and fan-favorite status in All Elite Wrestling.

stories.title: WWE releases multiple NXT and developmental talents in roster purge
stories.tldr: WWE has initiated a major roster purge targeting its developmental system, releasing ten NXT, Evolve, LFG, and Performance Center talents. Confirmed departures include former WWE Speed Champion Jasper Troy, long-tenured star Wendy Choo, and fan favorite Adriana Rizzo, alongside several newer prospects and a referee. Affected developmental wrestlers are subject to a standard 30-day non-compete clause rather than the main roster's 90-day window.

stories.title: Details on Rusev's absence from WWE TV due to medical issue
stories.tldr: Rusev has been absent from WWE television since his July 27 match against Je'Von Evans due to a neck injury and subsequent illness, debunking rumors that he had stormed off out of frustration. During the bout, he landed awkwardly on his neck causing his hands to go numb, but he chose to finish the match before being placed in concussion protocol. After a few weeks off, he returned to the Performance Center but was further delayed by an undisclosed illness. He was recently at the Performance Center to complete the medical clearance process and is expected to return to television this September.

stories.title: Matches and title bouts announced for WWE SmackDown in Mexico City
stories.tldr: WWE is loading up the September 11, 2026 episode of SmackDown from Arena CDMX in Mexico City with a massive card featuring multiple championship bouts and a heated grudge match. CM Punk will defend the Undisputed WWE Championship against Sami Zayn, while Chelsea Green puts the WWE Women's Championship on the line against Nia Jax. Additionally, Lucha Libre AAA partnerships continue as Rey Fénix defends his cruiserweight title against Ricky Saints and The War Raiders defend the tag team titles against Damian Priest and R-Truth, alongside a personal clash between Paige and Nikki Bella.

stories.title: John Cena reflects on his WWE heel turn and retirement tour
stories.tldr: John Cena is reflecting on his controversial 2025 WWE heel turn and final retirement tour, admitting that while the creative execution faced heavy criticism, the run was an undeniable success from a business standpoint. The idea was originally pitched by Paul Triple H Levesque, prompting Cena to agree instantly as part of his philosophy of taking bold risks. Though he accepts the critiques regarding both the storyline and his final match against Gunther, Cena has no regrets about swinging for the fences during his farewell.

stories.title: CM Punk, Johnny Gargano, and Sami Zayn involved in WWE Title picture on SmackDown
stories.tldr: On the September 4 episode of WWE SmackDown in Cleveland, CM Punk successfully defended his Undisputed WWE Championship against Johnny Gargano, who finally ended his long-running backstage motionless gag to accept the impromptu challenge. Sami Zayn heavily interfered in the main event, continuing his campaign of chaos while demanding his own title opportunity after being repeatedly thwarted. Consequently, an exasperated Punk challenged Zayn to a title match for the following week in Mexico City amidst a chaotic scene involving several top contenders.

stories.title: Joe Hendry announces release date for debut album 'Beyond Belief'
stories.tldr: WWE star Joe Hendry has officially announced that his debut album, Beyond Belief, will be released on October 5. The announcement was made during a television broadcast before he threw out the ceremonial first pitch at a New York Mets game at Citi Field. Hendry recorded the project primarily at WWE Studios and his home setup, blending his long-standing musical persona with his current run on the Raw brand.

stories.title: Mickie James reveals why she almost turned down 2022 WWE Royal Rumble return
stories.tldr: Mickie James recently revealed that she initially almost turned down an invitation to enter the 2022 WWE Women's Royal Rumble because she was still angry about her 2021 release and how her belongings were handled. She ultimately reconsidered on the condition that she could appear as the reigning TNA Knockouts Champion under her Hardcore Country persona instead of her previous WWE gimmick. During the same interview, she also reflected on a terrifying 2007 Falls Count Anywhere match against Melina where a freak accident led her to fear she had broken her neck.

stories.title: Baron Corbin explains why he didn't beg for his WWE job back before returning
stories.tldr: Reigning WWE United States Champion Baron Corbin recently discussed his departure and eventual return to the company, revealing he never once asked for his job back during his time away. Although he maintained friendly personal communication with Paul Triple H Levesque and several talents, he intentionally avoided discussing a professional comeback because he refused to beg for employment. WWE ultimately approached him in December 2025, but Corbin was in no rush to accept as he was busy traveling the world, winning titles, and sharpening his in-ring skills on the independent scene. He eventually returned to television, began a program with Trick Williams, and captured the United States Championship.

stories.title: Bakusai (Shinsuke Nakamura & Kyoki) win WWE SmackDown tag team debut
stories.tldr: Shinsuke Nakamura and his new tag team partner Kyoki, formerly known as NJPW star Hiromu Takahashi, successfully debuted as Bakusai on SmackDown by defeating The Miz and Kit Wilson. Immediately following their victory, the duo was confronted on stage by WWE Tag Team Champions the MFTs, featuring Talla, Tama Tonga, and their father Haku. This high-profile debut and subsequent confrontation set up an immediate championship feud aimed at revitalizing the SmackDown tag team division.

stories.title: Charlotte Flair speaks on daily battles over Ric Flair's social media posts
stories.tldr: Charlotte Flair recently appeared on Stephanie McMahon’s podcast to discuss her relationship with her father, WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair. She revealed that they engage in daily fights over his chaotic social media activity, ranging from all-caps posts to him arguing with obscure online accounts. Charlotte also has to routinely convince the 77-year-old legend that viral AI-generated images of himself are completely fake. Despite the digital headaches, she acknowledges that Ric is her biggest fan and joked that she wishes he would just let her manage his accounts.

stories.title: Stephanie McMahon reflects on identity struggles after leaving WWE executive post
stories.tldr: Stephanie McMahon recently opened up on her podcast about the identity struggles and questions of self-worth she experienced after stepping away from her corporate role as WWE co-CEO in January 2023. During an episode featuring guest Charlotte Flair, McMahon reflected on the initial difficulty of transitioning out of a working executive position and separating her personal value from her job title. Over time, she has learned to let go of the pressure to constantly prove herself, choosing instead to focus her energy on her family and enjoy life. Despite no longer holding an executive post, McMahon remains connected to the industry through her podcast, was inducted into the Hall of Fame, and maintains a deep, lifelong love for the wrestling business.

stories.title: Nikki Bella and Paige trade personal insults following SmackDown
stories.tldr: Following the September 4 episode of WWE SmackDown, Nikki Bella and Paige engaged in a deeply personal backstage war of words that quickly crossed the line from professional wrestling to real-life history. Paige targeted Nikki by referencing her past relationship with John Cena and mocking her divorce, delivering a scathing promo that used Cena's famous catchphrase. In response, Nikki took to social media to promise retribution as the feud heads toward a high-stakes showdown in Mexico City. The heated exchange has sparked intense debate among wrestling fans regarding whether the personal attacks went too far.

stories.title: John Cena defends Gunther's WWE booking after retiring him
stories.tldr: John Cena has defended Gunther's recent WWE booking following fan criticism regarding the star's trajectory since retiring both Cena and AJ Styles. In a recent interview, Cena explained that a wrestler's career moves in a non-linear fashion and that not every match can feature a legendary retirement. He also used the discussion to offer advice to younger talent dealing with career frustration and previewed his upcoming John Cena Classic tournament.

stories.title: Former referee Mike Chioda claims WWE removed his video game likeness over royalties
stories.tldr: Former long-time WWE referee Mike Chioda recently claimed that the company removed his likeness from its video games following a dispute over unpaid royalties. Chioda stated that after initially receiving substantial payouts arranged by Jim Ross, the checks stopped once John Laurinaitis took on a larger role in talent relations. When Chioda questioned why referees were not receiving royalties like the wrestlers, he was allegedly replaced in the subsequent game by an office employee paid a fraction of the cost. Chioda acknowledges that his removal being directly tied to his questioning is his own interpretation, as he lacks official documentation from the company.

stories.title: John Morrison details Bad Bunny's dedication to WWE training
stories.tldr: Former WWE star John Morrison recently praised Bad Bunny during an interview on The Wrestling Classic, highlighting the Grammy-winning artist's incredible dedication and humility during his time with the company. Morrison revealed that the massive music star was so respectful of professional wrestling that he actually canceled some of his concerts and relocated to Orlando to train full-time at the WWE Performance Center.
